headline: High-risk default interaction: Dify can write and execute server-side tools while the paired content source has broad network egress, creating leakage and cascading-error exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Dify can ingest uploaded knowledge-base files and wire tools into agent/workflow flows, so attacker-controlled content could be treated as instructions. The paired content-writing agent has broad network egress but no explicit parsing surface, so the bridge is indirect rather than proven. Uncertainty about the exact handoff pushes this above low.
conditions: IF agent_a outputs text that agent_b later ingests as tool instructions or prompt context
IF agent_b processes uploaded files or knowledge-base content without provenance filtering
mitigations: Add a strict instruction/content separator in agent_b prompts
Disable automatic ingestion of agent_a outputs into agent_b workflows
Require human review before any tool call triggered by imported text
Tag all imported content with provenance metadata
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and prompt-firewall middleware

B_data_leakage.rationale: Dify explicitly handles conversation logs, knowledge-base files, and secrets/tool credentials, while the paired agent has broad network egress. That creates a plausible path for sensitive content to be sent outward if agent_a or agent_b forwards it. The profiles do not prove a shared filesystem, so this is medium rather than high.
conditions: IF agent_b stores sensitive conversation logs or knowledge-base files containing secrets
IF either agent forwards those contents through network egress to a third party
mitigations: Restrict agent_b to non-sensitive datasets
Turn off or redact conversation-log export paths
Review outbound destinations for agent_a
Rotate any exposed tool credentials
requires-engineering: enforce DLP on file and log egress

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Agent_b can write the filesystem, execute shells, and spawn subprocesses, while agent_a has broad network egress. Even without modify_git_state, overlapping write-and-execute capability on shared server-side resources can corrupt state or overwrite artifacts in default orchestration. The shared-state model in Dify increases the conflict risk.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same writable workspace or datastore
IF agent_b instances run concurrently without external locking
mitigations: Assign separate workspaces per agent
Serialize writes through a single queue
Disable shell execution for nonessential tasks
Add file-locking around shared artifacts
requires-engineering: implement transactional coordination for shared state

D_cascading_error.rationale: Dify’s agent/workflow tooling can act on upstream outputs, and its tool-use pattern wires tools into agent flows. If agent_a produces incorrect facts or malformed content, agent_b may treat them as authoritative and execute downstream actions. Because agent_b has shell and subprocess authority, the blast radius can be irreversible.
conditions: IF agent_a output is used as input to agent_b without verification
IF agent_b triggers tools or shell commands based on that output
mitigations: Insert a verification step before any downstream action
Require citations for factual claims before execution
Limit agent_b to read-only mode for imported outputs
Log and review all tool-triggering prompts
requires-engineering: add policy gates for action execution

E_compliance.rationale: Agent_b explicitly touches conversation logs, knowledge-base content, and model-provider/tool credentials, while agent_a is a content-writing source with broad egress. The profiles do not show a residency or certification mismatch, but they do show retention-sensitive data classes flowing through a network-capable pair, which is a compliance gap in default deployments.
conditions: IF conversation logs or knowledge-base files contain regulated or retention-sensitive data
IF outbound model-provider or tool traffic is not covered by the operator's policy
mitigations: Classify data before routing it into Dify
Minimize retention of conversation logs
Restrict tool credentials to least privilege
Review data-processing notices and DPAs
requires-engineering: add residency and retention policy enforcement
